newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville raises Mon peak-hour prices $1-3/MWh.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville raises Mon peak-hour prices $1-3/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration said Friday it raised its prices for daily surplus firm power during peak-demand hours on Monday by $1.00 to $3.00 per megwatt hour (MWh) to as high as $20.00.
Price offers from the federal power marketing agency for Saturday and Sunday were $13.00 to $16.00, slightly lower than recent weekday offers.
Off-peak prices for Monday were unchanged at $13.00, but rose to $18.00 ($17.00 non-firm) during hours 0700-0900 and 2200-2300 PDT, and to $20.00 ($19.00 non-firm) for 1000-2100.
For Friday, BPA offered firm and non-firm power at $17.00 per MWh between 1300 and 2100 PDT, $14.50 for hours 0800-1200 and 2200-2300 PDT, and $13.00 for hours 0100-0700 and the hour ending 2400.
The Portland, Ore.-based agency capped pre-scheduled firm sales for Monday at 200 MW for hours 1000 through 2100 PDT.

For Saturday through Monday, BPA also withdrew Southwest buyers from its offer to sell light-load hour hydropower at $9.00 MWh if it is used in place of thermal generation. But the offer is still available to Northwest buyers.
